Consider a right triangle inscribed in a semicircle of radius
$\frac{1}{3},$ as shown above. Find the greatest possible perimeter ${P}_{\text{max}}$ of the triangle. Do not round the answer.

${P}_{\text{max}}=$
 {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Let's call $l$ the length of one of the legs. By the Pythagorean theorem, the length of the other leg is $\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-{l}^{2}}.$

Therefore, the perimeter is given by

$$
P(l)=\frac{2}{3}+l+\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-{l}^{2}}.
$$

Since $l$ is the length of a leg of a right triangle whose hypotenuse is $\frac{2}{3},$ the permitted range of $l$ is $0<l<\frac{2}{3}.$

We want to maximize $P(l),$ so we need to compute the critical points. Taking the derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(l) & =1+\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{(-2l)}{\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-{l}^{2}}} \\  & =1-\frac{l}{\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-{l}^{2}}},\end{aligned}
$$

and solving ${P}^{′}(l)=0$ gives the following critical point:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{l}{\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-{l}^{2}}} & =0 \\ l & =\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-{l}^{2}} \\ 2{l}^{2} & =\frac{4}{9} \\ {l}^{2} & =\frac{2}{9} \\ l & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

All that's left now is to confirm that $l=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ does indeed give a maximum value of $P(l).$ To do this, we use the first derivative test. We write up a table of values:

| Interval | $(0,\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})$ | $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ | $(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3},\frac{2}{3})$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Test Point | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| ${P}^{′}$ | $+$ | $0$ | $-$ |
| $P$ | $↗$ | $\text{max}$ | $↘$ |

So, $l=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ gives the maximum, and the perimeter of the resulting triangle will be the largest possible.

Therefore, the greatest perimeter ${P}_{\text{max}}$ that a triangle can have is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{\text{max}}=P\,(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}) & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}+\sqrt{\frac{4}{9}-\frac{2}{9}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}+\sqrt{\frac{2}{9}} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}+\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(1+\sqrt{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
